simple.meaning: הָרֶה (hâreh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “pregnant.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 16:11. The surrounding context includes family, family line, Torah, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הָרֶה (H2030) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: הָרֶה (hâreh) / H2030 is traced through Genesis 16:11, Genesis 38:24, Genesis 38:25, Exodus 21:22 with generated occurrence evidence.

majorEvents.evidenceText: His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to giving birth. When she heard the news that God’s ark was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth; for her pains came on her.

timeline.evidenceText: Yahweh’s angel said to her, “Behold, you are with child, and will bear a son. You shall call his name Ishmael, because Yahweh has heard your affliction.
About three months later, Judah was told, “Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has played the prostitute. Moreover, behold, she is with child by prostitution.”
When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, “I am with child by the man who owns these.” She also said, “Please discern whose these are—the signet, and the cords, and the staff.”
“If men fight and hurt a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, and yet no harm follows, he shall be surely fined as much as the woman’s husband demands and the judges allow.

for, behold, you shall conceive and give birth to a son. No razor shall come on his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb. He shall begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.”

but he said to me, ‘Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink. Don’t eat any unclean thing, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb to the day of his death.’ ”

His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to giving birth. When she heard the news that God’s ark was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth; for her pains came on her.
The woman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, “I am with child.”
Hazael said, “Why do you weep, my lord?”

Then Menahem attacked Tiphsah, and all who were in it, and its border areas, from Tirzah. He attacked it because they didn’t open their gates to him, and he ripped up all their women who were with child.
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.* “Immanuel” means “God with us”.
Just as a woman with child, who draws near the time of her delivery,
because he didn’t kill me from the womb.
Behold, I will bring them from the north country,
Israel, return to Yahweh your God;

definitions.full: H2030. harah II. הָרָה adjective feminine pregnant — absolute ׳ה Gen 16:11 10 t.; construct הֲרַת Jer 20:17 ; plural construct הָרוֺת Amos 1:13 ; suffix הָרוֺתֶיהָ 2Kin 15:16 ; הָרֹתֵיהֶם 8:12 ; — pregnant , as attributive, ה ׳אִשָּׁה Exod 21:22 ; as predicate Gen 38:24 ( לִזְנוּנִים ), 38:25 ( לְאִישׁ ), 1Sam 4:19 ; 2Sam 11:5 ; Isa 7:14 (+ וְיֹלֶדֶת ); in phrase וְיֹלַדְתְּ הָרָה הִנָּךְ Gen 16:11 (on resemblance to Isa 7:14 compare Peters Hebraica. Apr. 1885, 243; Apr. 1886, 175 ), Judg 13:5 , 7 ; = substantive pregnant women, women with child Amos 1:13 ; 2Kin 8:12 ; 15:16 ; Jer 31:8 , and, in simile, Isa 26:17 ; once of womb עוֺלָם הֲרַת וְרַחְמָהּ Jer 20:17 . הֵרוֺן see הֵרָיוֺן below [ הָרִיָּה ] adjective feminine pregnant , only plural as substantive וְהָרִיּוֺתָיו Hosea 14:1 (compare Assyrian êriiâtê Jäger BAS i. 473 ).
